title: Real Madrid to be without left-back Alvaro Carreras vs. Manchester City in latest injury blow
content:
Real Madrid expect to be without first-choice left-back Alvaro Carreras for Wednesday’s Champions League match against Manchester City due to a calf injury.

Madrid confirmed on Monday that Carreras, 22, had undergone assessments which revealed a muscle injury to his right calf.

Madrid sources, speaking on the condition of anonymity, indicated the club expect him to be sidelined for around a week, ruling him out of Wednesday’s last-16 first leg at the Bernabeu and leaving him with a race to be fit for the return leg at the Etihad on March 17.

Madrid are already contending with a number of injury absentees ahead of the Champions League tie against City. The Athletic reported on Friday that midfielder Jude Bellingham will miss the match at the Bernabeu as he continues to recover from a hamstring injury. Forward Kylian Mbappe is also not expected to be available due to a knee sprain, having travelled to France last week for further tests on the issue.

Defender Eder Militao and forward Rodrygo are sidelined with long-term injuries, while defender David Alaba and midfielder Dani Ceballos are also out.

Carreras sustained the injury against Getafe on March 2, before missing Friday’s win over Celta Vigo through suspension. He has made 34 appearances in all competitions this season following his summer move from Benfica, providing two goals and two assists, and has started eight of Madrid’s 10 Champions League matches this term.

Ferland Mendy, who has featured just four times in all competitions this season following multiple spells out with muscular injuries, started Friday’s victory against Celta in Carreras’ absence and is likely to play again against City. Midfielder Eduardo Camavinga has also previously been deployed at left-back.
